- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.2) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- If model shows gradual upward drift (e.g., +0.01–0.03/day) with no recent spike, but true outcome shows sharp downward correction, adjust downward bias by 0.5–1.0 units in early horizon.
- After a model forecast spike (e.g., >64.0), true outcome often corrects downward with lag — apply a 3–5 day “cool-down” buffer before expecting continuation.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (0.2–0.8), model often overestimates mean — apply a 0.5–1.0 unit downward adjustment to 30d forecast mean.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes (e.g., -0.14, -0.20), model tends to underestimate true drop — add 0.3–0.7 unit buffer to downward correction.
- Model often underestimates early 30d true values when sentiment is positive — adjust forecast downward by 0.5–1.0 units for first 5–7 days if sentiment > 0.7.
- If model forecast is flat or slightly rising with sentiment < 0.2, true outcome often drops sharply — add 0.5–1.0 unit downward correction for first 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is volatile (e.g., alternating +0.8 and -0.2), model tends to overfit recent trends — smooth forecast with 3–5 day moving average or reduce slope.
